item.title: Introducing wiremock-micronaut
item.description:
WireMock and Micronaut are two things I really like, so it was only a matter of time before the two came together :)

Say hello to wiremock-micronaut, a small library that makes testing HTTP clients in Micronaut 5 apps a whole lot nicer.

The problem

Testing an HTTP client properly means standing up a WireMock server, getting its URL into your Micronaut config before the beans that need it are created, and then getting hold of the server in your test so you can stub things. None of that is hard on its own, but it is the same plumbing every time, and it is easy to get the ordering wrong.

item.title: Creating Hugo Blog Posts from Meetup Pages using Kotlin Script and JSoup
item.description:
The Dark Side of Running a Meetup Group

I really enjoy running the Brighton Kotlin and Brighton JUG meetup groups. It is purely selfish to be honest, I get to meet lots of interesting people and learn a lot from the speakers and attendees and generally geek out with like-minded people.

However, there is a lot of admin involved in running a meetup group, let alone two - especially when you decide to set up a dedicated blog for each of the meetup groups. Add that to a full time job and family commitments and it makes an interesting juggling act. So, inspired by Yannick, one of the organisers of the local PHP meetup, and the way he automates the updating of the website homepage, I decided that it was time for me to look at my setup.

item.title: BlinkyTape JUnit Testwatcher API Implementation
item.description:
Every so often I like to have a play around with a part of Junit that I haven’t used before, and I recently decided to look into the TestWatcher API.

I have to admit that I have been meaning to play with this for quite a while now…. I just haven’t really found a good use-case for it. Given that I decided to quit trying to find a good use-case and implement something nerdy instead.
